trickyParts: The new spellings are last resorts. lastResorts is consulted only when no writing reaches depth 1 under inlineMarkdown. Letting them compete freely churned 1644 documents and lost 892 fixed points.

The merge of sjawhar/legion#2373 had real conflicts. Main's search loop already picked the earliest writing of the greatest read-back depth, so the branch's rule folds into it. The branch's '\!' before a link gave way to main's beforeLabel escape.
Playwright on main now runs only phone-tagged rows on iphone, so the browser suite shows 11 rows (chromium), not the 22 seen before the merge.

orderMarks keeps codeInnermost inside keepingOpen, byReach and reopening: following is ordered with next as its active marks, and sharedOpenMarks reads that prefix, so moving codeInnermost to the end would change the order.
deviations: The plan's 'D-a churn and lost fixed points 0' does not hold against 452e4647, because main changed stored bytes between 452e4647 and b93381d3 (sjawhar/legion#2373 and others). The flagged documents give the same counts with head = main and 0 against main with head = this branch, so this branch adds none.
escapeDestination's fast path stays removed, as the spec's #2373 cleanup list asks, even though the simplify reviewers proposed restoring it for the allocation.
The flanked spelling the writer picks for 'p \~\a*~* q' is 'p ~\\a*~* q', the earliest of the greatest depth. It is not the 'p \~\\a*~* q' that the plan listed.
Review round 1: the reviewer's code-quality item (2), folding the three mark-order cases into one orderMarks, was judged not required by the reviewer and is not done.
openQuestions: Five address documents (for example '**www\.a!b@c.test/q?a=1&b=2<b> and more**') read differently in Go and the engine on main since sjawhar/legion#2373. Main stores them, and they are reported to the architect.
